name: Total War: ROME II - Emperor Edition

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh lock paired with a 40 fps cap gives the smoothest feel for this strategy title; medium textures and shadows keep the game looking good on the campaign map while staying stable in average-sized battles.

profiles.Summary: Total War: ROME II runs on the Steam Deck via Proton at a Playable rating, with the strategy/campaign layer being well within reach but large-scale battles with many units can stress the GPU and cause frame drops. The game's 2013 engine is relatively modest by modern standards, making 30–40 fps achievable at medium settings without heavy upscaling tricks.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck or ProtonDB detailed reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2013 PC requirements (minimum GPU ~GTX 460/560, recommended ~GTX 660), the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class), and the game's known engine characteristics. On your first run, check frame rates during a mid-game battle with Normal unit sizes — that is the most demanding scenario — and adjust settings or the profile accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load low during long campaign sessions; small unit sizes dramatically reduce CPU/GPU load during battles. Use the touchscreen or right trackpad for menu navigation.

KnownIssues: Small UI text and tooltips can be difficult to read on the 7-inch screen due to the game's PC-centric interface design.
Proton compatibility is rated silver/gold trending, meaning occasional launch or stability issues may require switching Proton versions.
No native controller support — on-screen menus and unit selection are best navigated with the touchscreen or trackpads.
Large late-game battles with high unit counts may cause noticeable frame drops below 30 fps even at low settings.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with high textures looks sharp on the campaign map and holds near 60 fps in most situations, but large battles with many units will dip to 35-45 fps — consider dropping Unit Size to Normal if late-game battles become choppy.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap gives the smoothest pacing for a turn-based/RTS hybrid; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough. Drop Unit Size to Small if late-game battles stutter.

profiles.Summary: Total War: ROME II runs on the Steam Deck via Proton at a Playable rating, with the strategy/campaign layer running smoothly but large real-time battles being the main performance bottleneck. The game's PC minimum spec (DX9, 512 MB GPU) is well below the Deck's capability, but large battles with many units can still stress the hardware significantly.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (well within Deck capability) and general knowledge of Total War engine behavior. On your first run, check frame rates during a large battle — if they dip below your cap, reduce Unit Size first, then Texture and Terrain Quality.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load low; small unit sizes greatly reduce battle CPU/GPU load. Campaign map should hold 30 fps comfortably; large battles may dip slightly.

KnownIssues: UI and text can be very small at 1280x800, requiring careful scaling adjustments in-game
Large late-game battles with many unit stacks can cause significant frame drops
ProtonDB tier is silver/trending gold, meaning some users report minor issues with multiplayer or specific campaign events
Controller/gamepad support is limited — mouse and keyboard via dock or touchscreen/trackpad recommended for full UI access

MaxPerformance.Notes: Campaign map and smaller battles will hit 60 fps; large battles with many units will drop to 40-50 fps even at max TDP. Shadow Quality kept at Medium as it has the largest performance cost for minimal visual gain.
